phases.name: GPP
phases.goal: Build general work capacity, tissue tolerance and a base of size and strength
phases.focus: Hypertrophy, Strength Endurance, Work Capacity, Accessory / Prehab
phases.notes: Longest runway before competition. Keep technique clean.

phases.name: SPP
phases.goal: Convert the base into sport-relevant strength and power
phases.notes: Exercise selection moves closer to sport demands.

phases.name: Pre-Competition
phases.focus: Max Strength, Power (Ballistic), Speed, Reactive / Plyometric
phases.notes: Fewer exercises, high quality, long rests.

phases.name: In-Season
phases.goal: Maintain strength and power around competition load
phases.notes: Short sessions. Avoid heavy soreness close to competition.

phases.name: Deload
phases.notes: Cut volume by roughly 40 to 50 percent.

types.name: Max Strength
types.intent: Heaviest work. Maximal effort, long rests.

types.name: Strength
types.intent: Build force with controlled bar speed.

types.name: Hypertrophy
types.intent: Build muscle. Sets close to failure (RIR 0-3).

types.name: Power (Olympic)
types.intent: Max intent. Stop sets when bar speed drops.

types.name: Power (Ballistic)
types.intent: Accelerate through the full range. Light, fast.

types.name: Volume (GVT)
types.intent: German Volume Training. Same load all sets.

notes: How phases and workout types work together

A block moves through phases. GPP (general preparation) builds work capacity and a base of size and strength. SPP (specific preparation) turns that base into sport relevant strength and power. Pre-Competition peaks strength, power and speed with fewer exercises. Deload recovers. On each Week tab you choose the phase at the top, then give every exercise a workout type. The type sets the sets, reps, %1RM and rest. The phase tells you which types to emphasise. For example, Hypertrophy and Strength Endurance suit GPP, while Strength, Power and Speed suit SPP. Use the Programme tab as your reference, and remember the ranges are guidelines rather than orders.
How to use RPE and RIR

RPE is how hard a set felt on a 1 to 10 scale. RIR is reps in reserve, the number of good reps you could still have done. RPE 10 is RIR 0, RPE 9 is RIR 1, RPE 8 is RIR 2, RPE 7 is RIR 3. Enter RPE for your hardest set of the exercise in the RPE column. Strength work sits mostly around RPE 7 to 9. Hypertrophy sets sit closer to RPE 8 to 10. Power and speed work should stay crisp and fast, so stop the set when bar speed or sprint speed drops, not when you are exhausted.

The Suggested column gives a starting weight from your heaviest logged lift and the %1RM for the workout type. It updates as soon as you log a heavier weight. As a guide, if you hit the top of the rep range on every set at RPE 8 or lower for two sessions in a row, add roughly 2.5 kg to upper body lifts or 5 kg to lower body lifts next time. If the Suggested weight looks low, check the Heaviest cell for that exercise. A single light high rep set can leave it lower than you expect, and you can overtype the weight you actually use.
What to do after a missed session

Do not try to cram a missed session into the next one. Skip it and carry on with the next day as planned. If you miss a whole week, repeat that week. If you miss two weeks or more, restart the block two weeks back and reduce the weights by about 10 percent for the first session, then build back up. A session counts as logged once reps are entered, so only log what you actually did.

Week 8 is a deload. Keep the exercises, keep the weights moderate and cut volume by roughly 40 to 50 percent, for example by doing fewer sets per exercise while keeping technique sharp. You should finish each session feeling fresher than when you started. If you feel run down earlier in the block, take the deload early, then continue. The Dashboard shows weekly volume so you can see the drop.

Heaviest column is blank: that exercise has no logged weight yet, so the sheet falls back to your starting max on the Start Here tab. Suggested column is blank: the exercise needs a workout type, and speed and plyometric types are not loaded by weight. Exercise not counted: check the reps column has a number and at least one set has a weight (use 0 for bodyweight). Reps dropped part way through: use the next row down and leave the exercise name blank. Need sets 6 to 10: click the + above column O. A new exercise does not appear in the PB Tracker: it appears once reps and a weight are logged for it. Dates: on a phone or in Google Sheets tapping the date cell opens a calendar.
typenote: Notes: ranges are guidelines, not prescriptions. Speed and plyometric work are loaded by distance, intent or contacts rather than %1RM, so no weight is suggested for those types. Percentages are applied to the heaviest weight lifted for that exercise (or the starting max on Start Here until one is logged).
